fact: ZICTA reports a Board assessment tour of Universal Access and Service Fund ICT projects in Muchinga, Northern and Luapula Provinces, evaluating how they bridge the connectivity gap in unserved and underserved communities.

ZICTA's Universal Access and Service Fund committee inspected Fund projects in Copperbelt and Northwestern Provinces that promote digital inclusion in underserved communities, including the Telecommunication Towers Programme.
system: Universal Access and Service Fund Telecommunication Towers Programme

fact: Machiya Tower in Mpongwe District, built in 2021 under the 24 Towers Project, provides broadband coverage to over 9,500 people, and Lisomona Tower in Masaiti District, completed in 2025 under the 51 Towers Project, delivers 2G, 3G and 4G within 15 km, per ZICTA's inspection.

The Smart Zambia Institute's Electronic Government Division installed Starlink satellite internet kits in Moomba Chiefdom, Kazungula District, as part of the government's efforts to bring internet connectivity to rural communities.

fact: The Smart Zambia Institute's rollout connected three rural community institutions in Moomba Chiefdom: Moomba Rural Health Clinic, Choonzo Primary School and Kalamba Primary School.

fact: ZICTA's director of universal access said 43 of 51 remote-area towers were complete in September 2025, within a government rollout of 152 towers with Airtel and IHS Zambia, 40 of them operational.

The Ministry of Science and Technology's permanent secretary said in November 2024 that the Universal Access and Services Fund has been reaching unserved and underserved areas and can finance only about 30 towers a year against a deficit of about 900.

Smart Zambia Institute's coordinator says the World Bank-supported Digital Zambia Acceleration Project plans 300 communication towers, and Minister Mutati calls for more towers, particularly in underserved areas.
